facts.text: Lone Tree earned its name from a massive elm that once stood on a hill south of town, where buffalo grazed under its branches.
That elm survived prairie fires because the grass around it was scarce, a rare natural protection in the region.
In the 1960s Dutch Elm disease killed the tree, but locals salvaged its wood to craft a sign marking its former spot.
The Lone Tree Historical Society, founded in 1976, preserves the town’s past through collections, research, and public education.
A historic building donated to the society was renovated to house its museum, offering visitors a glimpse into local heritage.
The society’s research center holds genealogical records, maps, and local history books, making it a key resource for anyone curious about Lone Tree.
